title: Erdős Problem #20 — Exponential bound for families with no $k$-set sunflower
statement:
A family of sets $A_i$, $i = 1, 2, \ldots,$ is called a strong $\Delta$-system if all the intersections $A_i \cap A_j$ ($i \neq j$) are identical, i.e., if $A_i \cap A_j = \bigcap_i A_i$. Rado and I [40, 41] investigated the following question: Denote by $f_s(n,k)$ the smallest integer for which every family of sets $A_i$ ($1 \leq i \leq f_s(n,k)$) with $|A_i| = n$ for all $i$ contains $k$ sets which form a strong $\Delta$-system. Rado and I conjectured
$$f_s(n,3) < c_3^n$$
and no doubt also
$$f_s(n,k) < c_k^n.$$
I offer 1000 dollars for a proof or disproof of (11).
source_name: P. Erdős, Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry, Resenhas IME-USP 2 (1995), 165-186.
references: P. Erdős, Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry, Resenhas IME-USP 2 (1995), 165-186.

title: Successor conjecture for maximal projective-degree partitions
statement:
For each $n$, let $\lambda^{(n)}_{g\max}\models n$ be a partition of $n$ maximizing its projective degree $g^\lambda$. For a partition $\mu\models n$, define its set of $1$-successors by

$$
N(\mu,1)=\{\lambda\models n+1\mid |\lambda_i-\mu_i|\leq 1\text{ for }1\leq i\leq s\},
$$

where $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_s)$. **Successor conjecture.** For all $n$, the maximal projective-degree partition at size $n+1$ satisfies

$$
\lambda^{(n+1)}_{g\max}\in N(\lambda^{(n)}_{g\max},1).
$$

The claim extrapolates an observation verified computationally for $1\leq n<100$; when a maximum is not unique, the source specifies that every maximizer at size $n+1$ should be a $1$-successor of every maximizer at size $n$.
source_name: Dan Bernstein, “Strict Partitions of Maximal Projective Degree”, arXiv:0705.4015 (2007).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4015

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2007).

title: Mori's exact constant conjecture for planar quasiconformal maps
statement:
Let $QC_K$ be the family of all $K$-quasiconformal self-maps of the unit disk $\mathbf{B}^2$ that fix the origin, and let $M(2,K)$ be the least constant such that

$$
|f(x)-f(y)|\leq M(2,K)|x-y|^{K^{-1}},
$$

for every $f\in QC_K$ and $x,y\in\mathbf{B}^2$. **Mori's conjecture.**

$$
M(2,K)=16^{1-1/K}.
$$

The conjecture refines Mori's bound $M(2,K)\leq 16$ by incorporating the exact value at $K=1$; it was still open in 2009.
source_name: Barkat Ali Bhayo and Matti Vuorinen, “On Mori's theorem for quasiconformal maps in the n-space”, arXiv:0906.2853 (2011).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.2853

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2009). “On the other hand the trivial observation that $16$ fails to be a sharp constant for $K =1$ led to the following conjecture, which is still open in 2009.”

title: Richter and Salazar's bounded-bandwidth conjecture for crossing-critical graphs
statement: A graph is **$k$-crossing-critical** if its crossing number is at least $k$, but every proper subgraph has crossing number smaller than $k$. **Richter and Salazar's conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, there exists an integer $B(k)$ such that every $k$-crossing-critical graph has bandwidth at most $B(k)$. The source states that this conjecture, proposed as an open problem by Carsten Thomassen in the 1990s and formulated by Richter and Salazar, is disproved in the paper for every $k\geq 171$ by examples with arbitrarily large maximum degree; the abstract presents the two conjectures as disproved together.
source_name: Zdenek Dvorak and Bojan Mohar, “Crossing-critical graphs with large maximum degree”, arXiv:0907.1599 (2009).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.1599

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2009). “The second conjecture was proposed as an open problem in the 1990's by Carsten Thomassen and formulated as a conjecture by Richter and Salazar.”

title: Saturation number of $T_3^{\le 2}$
statement:
Let $T_3^{\le 2}$ denote the specified binary matrix family, and let $\operatorname{sat}(n,F)$ be the minimum number of columns in an $n$-row $F$-saturated matrix. Set $F=T_3^{\le 2}$. **The saturation conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{sat}(n,F)=10\quad\text{for every }n\ge 7.
$$

The paper constructs $F$-saturated matrices with ten columns for all $n\ge 7$, giving the upper bound. The equality is stated as a conjecture, so the corresponding lower bound remains open.
source_name: Andrzej Dudek, Oleg Pikhurko and Andrew Thomason, “On Minimum Saturated Matrices”, arXiv:0909.1970 (2012).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.1970

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2009).

title: A 12l upper bound for the height of the classical modular polynomial
statement:
Let $l$ be a prime, and let $\Phi_l$ denote the classical modular polynomial of prime level $l$. Its height $h(\Phi_l)$ is the logarithm of the maximum absolute value of its coefficients.

**Height upper-bound conjecture.** For every prime $l>30$,

$$
h(\Phi_l)<6l\log l+12l.
$$

This would improve the proven bound $h(\Phi_l)\leq 6l\log l+18l$ and is motivated by the numerical data in the paper; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source_name: Reinier Broker and Andrew V. Sutherland, “An explicit height bound for the classical modular polynomial”, arXiv:0909.3442 (2010).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.3442

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2009).

title: Tight upper-bound conjecture for admissible vertex counts of normal surfaces
statement:
Let $n$ be the number of tetrahedra in a triangulation, and let $\sigma$ denote its admissible vertex count. For positive $n\neq 1,2,3,5$, equation~ gives the proposed upper bound.

**Tight upper-bound conjecture.** For every positive $n\neq 1,2,3,5$, equation~ gives a tight upper bound on the admissible vertex count $\sigma$. Consequently,

$$
\sigma\in O(17^{n/4}).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the census, in which the pathological triangulations give the maximum observed admissible vertex counts wherever they are defined. It predicts the observed maximum growth rate, but the supplied text gives no resolution beyond these computational observations.
source_name: Benjamin A. Burton, “The complexity of the normal surface solution space”, arXiv:0911.5498 (2010).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.5498

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2009).

title: The maximum number of dismal divisors in base b
statement:
Let $d_b(n)$ denote the number of dismal divisors of $n$ in base $b$, and let $n$ range over the $k$-digit base-$b$ numbers. **Maximum-divisor conjecture.** For every base $b\geq 3$, $d_b(n)$ has a unique maximum at

$$
n=\frac{b^k-1}{b-1}=111\ldots1|_b.
$$

The claim identifies the all-ones base-$b$ number as the unique $k$-digit number with the most dismal divisors. The paper gives this as a conjecture after noting that these numbers come close to the general upper bound, and does not report a resolution.
source_name: David Applegate, Marc LeBrun and N. J. A. Sloane, “Dismal Arithmetic”, arXiv:1107.1130 (2011).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.1130

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2011).

title: Mubayi–Rödl conjecture on M-intersecting families with short integer intervals
statement:
Let $M\subset [n]:=\{0,\ldots,n\}$, and let $l(M)$ denote the maximum number of consecutive integers contained in $M$. Let $\mathcal{A}\subset 2^V$ be an $M$-intersecting family, meaning that $|A\cap B|\in M$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal{A}$. **Mubayi–Rödl conjecture.** If $1<l<n/10$ and $l(M)=l$, then

$$
|\mathcal{A}|<2^{n/2+o(n)}.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the Eventown-type upper bound remains valid when the longest interval of allowed intersection sizes has length less than $n/10$. The authors note that the constant $1/10$ is somewhat arbitrary, but that a restriction of this kind is needed to exclude constructions using families of sets of size at most $l-1$.
source_name: Dhruv Mubayi and Vojtech Rodl, “Specified Intersections”, arXiv:1107.5651 (2012).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.5651

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2011). “This was later proved by Frankl and F\"uredi for fixed $t$ (see also for related results).”

title: The conjectured minimum of the prime-indexed density constants
statement:
For each prime $p$, let $\delta_p$ denote the density constant associated with the set of $p$-Carmichael numbers, as defined by

$$
\delta_p:=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{|\mathfrak{C}_1\cap[1,n]|}{|\mathfrak{C}_p\cap[1,n]|}.
$$

**Density-minimum conjecture.**

$$
0.18<\delta_5<\delta_p\quad\text{for all prime }p\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{5\}.
$$

This conjecture predicts that $\delta_5$ is the smallest of the prime-indexed density constants and gives the numerical lower bound $0.18$. The existence of the relevant limits is part of the preceding conjectural framework and is not proved in the supplied text.
source_name: Antonio M. Oller-Marcén and José María Grau, “On the congruence _j=1^n-1 j^k(n-1) -1 n . k-strong Giuga and k-Carmichael numbers”, arXiv:1311.3522 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.3522

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2013).

title: Strict monotonicity conjecture for the minimum size of pancyclic graphs
statement:
Let $m(n)$ be the minimum number of edges in a pancyclic graph on $n$ vertices, where a pancyclic graph contains a cycle of every length $k$ with $3\leq k\leq n$. **Strict monotonicity conjecture.**

$$
m(n)<m(n+1)\quad\text{for all }n\geq 3.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the minimum number of edges required for pancyclicity strictly increases with the number of vertices. The paper establishes exact values for $m(n)$ through $n=37$ and proves the conjecture in some special cases; the general statement remains open.
source_name: Sean Griffin, “Minimal Pancyclicity”, arXiv:1312.0274 (2013).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1310.7825](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.7825).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.0274

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2013).

title: Erdős–Sós and Kalai's conjecture for Turán numbers of r-trees
statement:
Let $r\geq 2$, and let $T$ be an $r$-tree on $v$ vertices. An $r$-tree is an $r$-uniform hypergraph with edges $e_1,\ldots,e_q$ such that, for each $i$, there is some $k<i$ satisfying

$$
e_i\cap\left(\bigcup_{j<i}e_j\right)\subset e_k.
$$

Write ${\rm ex}_r(n,T)$ for the maximum number of edges in an $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices containing no copy of $T$. **Erdős–Sós–Kalai conjecture.** For every $r\geq 2$ and every $r$-tree $T$ on $v$ vertices,

$$
{\rm ex}_r(n,T)\leq \frac{v-r}{r}{n\choose r-1}.
$$

For $r=2$ this is the Erdős–Sós conjecture, while for $r\geq 3$ the source attributes it to Kalai (1984). The paper presents this as an open conjecture in its concluding remarks; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
source_name: Alexandr Kostochka, Dhruv Mubayi and Jacques Verstraete, “Turan Problems and Shadows II: Trees”, arXiv:1402.0544 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.0544

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

title: All-order upper-bound conjecture for complete arcs
statement:
Let $t_{2}(2,q)$ be the smallest size of a complete arc in $\mathrm{PG}(2,q)$, and let the bounds denoted in the source by 
$$
through
$$
 be the explicit upper bounds obtained from the computed complete arcs and lexiarcs. **All-order upper-bound conjecture.** These bounds hold for every prime power $q\geq109$.
The bounds are proved computationally for all prime powers through $301813$, with additional sporadic computations up to $430007$; the conjecture extrapolates their validity to all prime powers $q\geq109$.
source_name: Daniele Bartoli, Alexander A. Davydov, Giorgio Faina, Alexey A. Kreshchuk, Stefano Marcugini and Fernanda Pambianco, “Tables, bounds and graphics of sizes of complete arcs in the plane PG(2,q) for all q321007 and sporadic q in [323761430007] obtained by an algorithm with fixed order of points (FOP)”, arXiv:1404.0469 (2018).

title: Cocycle-invariant support conjecture for the Rig quandle Q(12,6)
statement:
Let $X=Q(12,6)$, let $A=\mathbb{Z}_4$, and let $\phi:X\times X\rightarrow A$ be the generating $2$-cocycle chosen in the source's example. For a knot $K$, let $\Phi_\phi(K)$ denote its quandle cocycle invariant in $\mathbb{Z}[A]$, with $u$ representing a generator of $A$. **Q(12,6) cocycle-invariant conjecture.** For every knot $K$,

$$
\Phi_\phi(K)=a+bu^2,
$$

where $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$. Computations through nine crossings exhibit only the constant and $u^2$ terms, and the source conjectures that this holds for all knots.
source_name: W. Edwin Clark, M. Saito and L. Vendramin, “Quandle coloring and cocycle invariants of composite knots and abelian extensions”, arXiv:1407.5803 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5803

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2014).

title: The maximal Schubert specialization conjecture for Richardson permutations
statement: For a given $n$, let $S_n$ be the symmetric group and let ${\mathfrak{S}}_w$ denote the Schubert polynomial associated with a permutation $w\in S_n$. Consider the specialization ${\mathfrak{S}}_w(1,\dots,1)$. **Richardson-permutation conjecture.** The permutation $w\in S_n$ with the largest value of ${\mathfrak{S}}_w(1,\dots,1)$ is Richardson. The claim is motivated by computations for all permutations with $n\leq 10$, where the maximum was always attained at a Richardson permutation. Geometrically, this specialization is the degree of the corresponding matrix Schubert variety and, under the stated condition, the multiplicity of a singular point of a Schubert variety; the conjecture therefore predicts that a Richardson permutation yields the worst singularities in this sense.
source_name: Grigory Merzon and Evgeny Smirnov, “Determinantal identities for flagged Schur and Schubert polynomials”, arXiv:1410.6857 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.6857

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2014).

title: RRP codes exceed the LMRD bound outside the exceptional packet lengths
statement:
Let $v$ be a packet length, and let the **RRP** denote the construction problem referred to in the source. The **LMRD code bound** is the benchmark bound for lifted maximum-rank-distance codes; the echelon-Ferrers construction and its variants are competing constructions.

**RRP bound conjecture.** For any packet length $v\geq 7$ with $v\notin\{8,10\}$, the largest subspace codes that can be obtained by solving the RRP exceed the LMRD code bound and thus are better than the codes resulting from the echelon-Ferrers construction and its variants.

The claim is motivated by computational results for packet lengths through $15$, but the supplied text does not establish it for every stated $v$ and gives no resolution beyond those computations.
source_name: Jingmei Ai, Thomas Honold and Haiteng Liu, “The Expurgation-Augmentation Method for Constructing Good Plane Subspace Codes”, arXiv:1601.01502 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.01502

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).

title: Conjecture on avoiding primes for elementary symmetric Boolean functions
statement:
Let $\sigma_{n,k}$ be the elementary symmetric Boolean function of degree $k$ in $n$ variables, and let $S(\sigma_{n,k})$ denote its exponential sum. Suppose that $k$ is a natural number that is not a power of two. Define $r$ by

$$
2^{r-1}<k<2^r
$$

and let $\mathfrak{p}(k)$ be the smallest prime $p$ of the form $p=2^r m+1$, with $m$ a positive integer, such that the sequence $\{S(\sigma_{n,k})\}$ avoids $p$. **Avoiding-prime conjecture.** The prime $\mathfrak{p}(k)$ exists. The existence of such a prime for every non-power-of-two degree would imply the Cusick–Li–Stănică conjecture; the source reports verification for all non-powers of two in the range $1<k<2048$, but does not state a general proof.
source_name: Francis N. Castro and Luis A. Medina, “Modular periodicity of exponential sums of symmetric Boolean functions and some of its consequences”, arXiv:1603.00534 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.00534

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2016).

title: Conjecture on the maximum length of rich square-free words
statement:
Let $r(n)$ be the maximum length of a rich square-free word over an alphabet of size $n$, and let $w_n$ be the recursively constructed rich square-free word over an alphabet of size $n$. **Conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$,

$$
r(n)=\operatorname{max}\\{|w_n|,2\cdot|w_{n-1}|+1\\}.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the maximum length is the larger of the length of the paper's recursively constructed word and the length obtained from the basic recursion. The computed values for $n=7,8,9,10$ motivate the conjecture, but the exact values for $n=8$ and $n=9$ were not computable in the paper.
source_name: Jetro Vesti, “Rich square-free words”, arXiv:1603.01058 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.01058

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2016).

title: Nordhaus–Gaddum product lower-bound conjecture for the Hadwiger number
statement:
Let $G_1,\ldots,G_r$ be graphs on a common vertex set of size $n$, whose edge sets partition the edges of $K_n$, and let $\ngpl{\eta}(r;n)$ denote the minimum of $\prod_{i=1}^r\eta(G_i)$ over all such $r$-decompositions, where $\eta(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$. **Product lower-bound conjecture.** For all $r\geq 2$ and $n\geq 1$,

$$
\ngpl{\eta}(r;n)=n.
$$

The source notes that this conjecture is implied by Hadwiger's conjecture. The paper proves only the bounds $(0.513)^{r-2}n\leq\ngpl{\eta}(r;n)\leq n$.
source_name: Leslie Hogben, Jephian C. -H. Lin and Michael Young, “Multi-part Nordhaus-Gaddum type problems for tree-width, Colin de Verdière type parameters, and Hadwiger number”, arXiv:1604.08817 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.08817

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2016).

title: Tame reduction to the trivial multifraction for Artin-Tits monoids
statement:
Let $M$ be an Artin–Tits monoid, let $\mathcal{F}_{M}$ be the set of multifractions over $M$, and let $\operatorname{red}_{\mathrm{t}}$ denote tame reduction. A multifraction is **unital** if it represents the identity in the enveloping group of $M$, and $\underline{1}$ denotes the trivial multifraction. **Tame-reduction conjecture.** For every unital multifraction $\underline{a}\in\mathcal{F}_{M}$, one has

$$
\operatorname{red}_{\mathrm{t}}(\underline{a})=\underline{1}.
$$

This conjecture concerns a weaker, restricted reduction procedure. The supplied text reports that no counterexample had been found for Artin–Tits monoids, but the conjecture is not marked as resolved.
source_name: Patrick Dehornoy, “Multifraction reduction II: Conjectures for Artin-Tits groups”, arXiv:1606.08995 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08995

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2016); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Nonexistence of infinite finitely generated solvable groups with square-free generalized identity length
statement: Let $G$ be an infinite finitely generated solvable group, and let $n$ be a square-free integer. **Nonexistence conjecture.** There are no such groups $G$ satisfying a generalized identity of length $n$. The surrounding results construct infinite finitely presented metabelian examples when $p^2\mid n$ for a prime $p$, while the square-free case is left unresolved in the supplied text.
source_name: Júlia Kato and Douglas V. P. Silva, “Generalized torsion in triangular matrix groups”, arXiv:2606.10168 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10168

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

title: Faber-Krahn for Dirac operator with infinite mass boundary condition
statement:
Prove or disprove that among all planar domains of a given area, the disk is the unique minimizer for the smallest positive eigenvalue
$\nu_1(\Omega)$ of the Dirac problem
with infinite mass boundary conditions

$$
\left\{
\begin{aligned}
	-\mathsf{i}
\big(\partial_1 v - \mathsf{i}\partial_2 v\big) &= \nu u 
	&&\text{in} \quad \Omega \,,
 \\
 -\mathsf{i}\big(\partial_1 u + \mathsf{i}\partial_2 u\big) 
&= \nu v 
 &&\text{in} \quad \Omega \,,
 \\
 \mathsf{i}\big(n_1 + \mathsf{i} n_2\big) u
 &= v
 &&\text{on} \quad \partial\Omega \,,
 \end{aligned}
 \right.
$$

 where~$n = (n_1,n_2)^\top$ is the outer unit normal to~$\Omega$.
source_name: AimPL: Shape optimization with surface interactions (posed by T. Ourmières-Bonafos)

title: Failure of MC
statement:
Show that Monte-Carlo fails on the SBM below the KS bound. This is related to the quantity $Z(\alpha) = \sum_{\tau: \alpha(\sigma,\tau) \approx \alpha} P(G | \tau)$. We want to understand $\mathbb{E}_{G | \sigma} \log Z(\alpha)$. Here $\sigma$ and $\tau$ are colorings of the vertices and $\alpha$ is the overlap matrix

$$
\alpha_{rs} = \frac{|\sigma^{-1}(r) \cap \tau^{-1}(s)|}{n/k}.
$$

It is tractible to compute the annealed average $\mathbb{E}_{G | \sigma} Z(\alpha)$. Is this quantity related?
source_name: AimPL: Connecting communities via the block model (posed by Cris Moore)

title: Problems (problem 4)
statement:
Let $X \sim MVN(\theta, I_d)$, where $I_d$ denotes the $d$-dimensional identity matrix. Consider the problem of estimating $\theta$ using estimators of the form $X + h(X)$, where $h$ is in some class $\mathcal{H}$ of functions. By SURE,

$$
\hat{r}_h = d + 2\nabla \cdot h(X) + \|h(X)\|^2
$$

is an unbiased estimator of the risk associated with $h$. Let

$$
h^* &= \text{arg min} (h \in \mathcal{H}: \hat{r}_h) \\
\hat{\theta}^* &= X + h^*(X).
$$

Find an unbiased estimator $r^{**}$ of the risk $\mathbb{E}(\|\hat{\theta}^* - \theta\|^2)$ of $\hat{\theta}^*$.
source_name: AimPL: Stein's method and applications in high-dimensional statistics (posed by Persi Diaconis)

title: Crossings in random square tilings
statement: Tile the unit square by finitely or countably many squares of varying sizes, with at most three squares meeting at a corner, and color the squares independently black or white with equal probabilities. Prove that the probability of a black left-to-right crossing is bounded below by a universal constant $c>0$. Moreover, as the largest tile diameter tends to zero, does this crossing probability tend to $1/2$?
source_name: Benjamini - Percolation and Coarse Conformal Uniformization (proposed by Itai Benjamini)

title: Problem 2.17 — (Nonarithmetic extremal surfaces).
statement: (Nonarithmetic extremal surfaces). Give answers to all of the above problems on automorphisms of Riemann surfaces for the collection of non-arithmetic surfaces. For example find bounds on orders of automorphism groups which are nilpotent, solvable, p-groups, etc. Prove that these bounds are sharp for infinitely many g. Determine the frequency of those g for which such bounds are sharp. Determine the least genus for which the bounds are sharp. The model result for these kind of problems is the following.
source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics

title: Does every separated Noetherian scheme have the resolution property?
statement:
A Noetherian scheme $X$ has the **resolution property** if every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ admits a surjection
$$
\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F
$$
from a finite-rank vector bundle $\mathcal E$. This asks for a single vector-bundle quotient, not a finite locally free resolution.

**Open problem.** Does every separated Noetherian scheme have the resolution property? Equivalently, can one construct such an $X$ and a coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$ that is not a quotient of any finite-rank vector bundle? More sharply, does every proper scheme over a field have the resolution property?

**Known boundary.** The property holds for schemes with an ample family of line bundles, a class that includes quasi-projective schemes and regular separated Noetherian schemes. Gross proved it for every separated surface of finite type over a field. Mathur and Schröer proved that a reduced separated excellent scheme has the property away from a closed subset of codimension at least three.

Thus a finite-type counterexample over a field would have to be singular, non-quasi-projective, and at least three-dimensional; a proper counterexample would also have to be nonprojective. The proper case is still explicitly listed as open by the Stacks Project.
references:
The Stacks Project, *The resolution property*, Tag 0F85. https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F85
B. Totaro, *The resolution property for schemes and stacks*, J. Reine Angew. Math. 577 (2004), 1–22. https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0207210
P. Gross, *The resolution property of algebraic surfaces*, Compos. Math. 148 (2012), 209–226. https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.2206
S. Mathur and S. Schröer, *The resolution property holds away from codimension three*, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 376 (2023), 1041–1063. https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09623

title: Hypercentre and finite conjugacy centre of unit groups of group rings
statement: Let $G$ be a group, let $Z^{\infty}(G)$ denote the union of the terms of the upper central series of $G$, and set $U=U(\mathbb ZG)$. Is $Z^{\infty}(U)\leq \Delta(U)$? Is $\Delta(U)\leq N_U(G)$? Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional simple $\mathbb Q$-algebra and let $\Gamma$ be a $\mathbb Z$-order in $A$. Determine the finite conjugacy centre $\Delta(U(\Gamma))$ of the unit group $U(\Gamma)$. Determine the same object for a Wedderburn component $A$ of $\mathbb QG$, where $G$ is the counterexample to the normalizer problem given by M. Hertweck. When $\Gamma$ contains the projection $\overline G$ of $G$ onto $A$, also determine the normalizer $N_{U(\Gamma)}(\overline G)$.
source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2007/55, page 26
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2007/55](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1738), page 26. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Formal analysis of locality, sparsity, and local maxima for bounded biharmonic weights
statement: For the bounded biharmonic weights w_j defined as minimizers of the Laplacian energy subject to the handle interpolation, cage-face linearity, partition-of-unity, and bounds in equations (2)\(6) of the report, formally prove or disprove the experimentally observed properties of locality, sparsity, and absence of local maxima. In the report, locality informally means that if a locally shortest shape-aware path from a point to a handle passes near another handle, the first handle's weight should vanish at that point; sparsity means that each point should be influenced by only a few nearby handles; and absence of local maxima means that each weight should attain its global maximum value 1 on its handle and have no other local maxima.

title: Strict positivity of the Green–Kubo conductivity with positive coupling and noise
statement:
For the chain of Hamiltonian cells perturbed by an energy-preserving noise of intensity $\varsigma>0$ and coupled by a smooth nearest-neighbor potential of strength $\varepsilon$, prove or disprove the conjecture that
\[
\kappa(\varepsilon,\varsigma)>0\qquad\text{whenever }\varepsilon>0\text{ and }\varsigma>0.
\]
Equivalently, under the report’s setup, determine whether there are no stable heat insulators when both the coupling and the noise are positive.

title: Narayana numbers in an identity involving semistandard Young tableaux
statement:
For integers $m\ge r\ge l\ge 1$ and $1\le \beta<m$, let $\operatorname{SSYT}_{r,l}(m)$ denote the number of semistandard Young tableaux of shape consisting of two columns of lengths $r\ge l$, with no entry exceeding $m$. Let $Y_{r,l}^{\beta}(m)$ denote the number of such tableaux in which the number $\beta$ appears somewhere in the second column. The identity

$$Y_{r,l}^{\beta}(m)=\sum_{1\le f\le e\le\beta}N_{e-1,f-1}\,\operatorname{SSYT}_{r-f,l-f}(m-e),$$

where

$$N_{e,f}=\frac{1}{e}\binom{e}{f+1}\binom{e}{f},$$

has a recursive proof. Find a proof of the formula that explains the occurrence of the Narayana numbers.

title: Sharp minimax rates for structured matrix estimation and matrix completion
statement:
For the structured matrix-estimation problem in model (3), over the class $\Theta$ defined in (2), determine whether the lower-bound rate in Theorem 1 is the minimax rate of convergence. In particular, under the theorem's conventions and hypotheses, including i.i.d. Gaussian noise, the rate should be of order
$$
\frac{\sigma^2}{p}\left(R_X+R_B+R_Z\right),
$$
where $R_X=n r_m\wedge n s_n\log(ek_n/s_n)$, $R_B=r_n r_m$, $R_Z=m r_n\wedge m s_m\log(ek_m/s_m)$, $r_n=n\wedge k_n$, and $r_m=m\wedge k_m$, with the corresponding $R_X$ or $R_Z$ term omitted when $A_{s_n}$ or $A_{s_m}$ is the identity matrix.

title: Non-random unitary-matrix examples for a minimum output entropy counterexample
statement:
Can one find a constant $C>0$, an integer $k>\\exp(2C^2)$, and unitary matrices $U_1,\ldots,U_k\in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ such that, for any $n^2$ matrix coefficients $a_{ij}$, 
$$
\left\|\sum_{i\ne j} a_{ij}U_iU_j^*\right\|\le C\sqrt{\sum_{i\ne j}|a_{ij}|^2}
$$
where the norm is the operator norm on the matrices? The requested examples are to be non-random; any such example would give a counterexample to the minimum output entropy additivity conjecture.

title: Does vertex percolation preserve max cut?
statement:
Let $G=G_n$ be a sequence of graphs with $e(G)/v(G)\to\infty$. Let $S$ be a random subset of $V(G)$ in which every vertex is included independently with probability $1/2$. Prove or disprove that, with probability $1-o(1)$,

$$\frac{\operatorname{maxcut}(G[S])}{e(G[S])}=\frac{\operatorname{maxcut}(G)}{e(G)}+o(1).$$

Here $G[S]$ is the subgraph induced by $S$, and $\operatorname{maxcut}(G)$ is the maximum number of edges of a bipartite subgraph of $G$.

title: Deriving Nekrasov’s blow-up formula from a coset VOA decomposition
statement:
Prove the blow-up formula

$$
\Psi(a,m;w,q;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}\Psi(a+\epsilon_1 n,m;w,q;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2-\epsilon_1)\,Z(a+\epsilon_2 n,m;q;\epsilon_1-\epsilon_2,\epsilon_2)
$$

as a consequence of the VOA representation identity

$$
V_{h,k}\otimes V_{0,1}=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb Z}V_{h+2n,k+1}\otimes W_{P+nb,b},
$$

assuming the parameter relations displayed in (4), together with

$$
\frac{\epsilon_1-\epsilon_2}{\epsilon_2}=b^2=-\frac{k+3}{k+2}.
$$

The derivation must also determine the precise relative normalizations of the conformal blocks occurring in the blow-up formula.

title: Combinatorial explanation of a three-quarter-plane walk identity
statement:

\[
w_{2,1,n}=2w_{1,2,n}.
\]
